Conor Williams: Williams has the physical profile and tape of a franchise left tackle. The highly regarded Texas recruit looks capable of holding down the blind side for a decade, making him the early standard for offensive linemen in this class as scouts return to the tape.
James Rodriquez: Rodriquez pairs a big frame with the instincts to find the football quickly. The former five-star recruit has produced every year at Ohio State, and his athleticism and feel for zone coverage give him a role beyond stopping the run.
Mikael Thomas: Thomas covers ground in zone and knows what to do when the throw comes his way. The Clemson corner’s range and ball skills let him turn a contested pass into a takeaway, giving him a knack for changing possessions when quarterbacks challenge his area.
Jordan Nunez: At 6-foot-8 and 320 pounds, Nunez gives Notre Dame a powerful presence at tackle. He has the strength to control defenders and the versatility to play on either side, offering the profile of a long-term starter on the edge of an offensive line.
Neville Gibson: Gibson brings both force as a hitter and the hands to finish an interception. A former five-star recruit and captain of a talented Ohio State defense, he enters the season as a safety who can make plays through contact or in coverage.
Ryan Hodges III: Hodges returned to Ohio State with a chance to raise his draft stock. His soft hands and unusually large catch radius help him make difficult grabs look routine, giving quarterbacks room to throw even when the window appears tight or the ball arrives off target.
Taylen Ingram: Ingram threatens defenses with vertical speed and becomes just as dangerous once the ball reaches him. The Florida receiver has a slight frame, but his contact balance helps him stay on his feet and keep a play alive after the first hit.
Brennan Coombs: Coombs approaches defense like a quarterback, using his understanding of the game to direct the players around him. The Texas A&M standout enters the season among the nation’s top linebackers and has the leadership profile to take charge of a defense early in his career.
C.J. Nielsen: Nielsen opens the season as the leading quarterback in a thin class. The 6-foot-4 Ole Miss passer works comfortably from the pocket and throws with anticipation, giving a team in need of a starter a clear set of traits to evaluate.
Alex Martinez: Martinez led Ohio State in touchdown catches in his first year as a starter. The former five-star recruit brings the athleticism to be a featured target at tight end, and that early production gives him a strong base heading into the season.
